text.p: Here are the highlights from Swiss newspapers on Monday:
- Nazis managed to gain access to information about numbered Swiss bank accounts belonging to Jews during World War Two, according to U.S. Senator Alfonse D'Amato.
- Nearly 233,500 new automobiles were sold in Switzerland in the first 10 months of the year, 1.8 percent fewer than in the same period last year.
- Basle-based pharmaceuticals firm Sandoz was granted German permission to buy Azupharma, a subsidiary of Gehe AG.
- TAG Heuer, a manufacturer of luxury watches, posted a sales increase of 9.8 percent to 317 million Swiss francs for the first three quarters of the year, compared to the previous year.
- Ski lift ticket prices will not be increased in Switzerland for the second season in a row.
- Saudi Arabia's King Fahd received permission to expand the buildings of "vacation village" in Collonge-Bellerive, near Geneva.
- Swiss Rentenanstalt/Swiss Life is buying the Belgian subsidiary of France's state-run insurance group Groupement des Assurances Nationales for 140 million Swiss francs.
